title: P5 Provider Registry and Custom Provider UX
goal: Integrate the three verified adapters behind a safe service/protocol registry and complete native and Custom Provider configuration UX.

facts.text: Provider IDs currently include OpenAI, OpenRouter and Custom OpenAI-compatible, while endpoint profiles are fixed to Chat Completions.
The provider gate and background wiring are hard-coded to the OpenAI-compatible factory.
Options already presents service, model, API Key, test connection, disclosure and Custom Base URL.
Credential eligibility binds provider and origin, while capability identity also includes endpoint path, profile, model and credential revision.

in: Native OpenAI Responses, OpenRouter Chat and Anthropic Messages profiles
Custom Chat or Responses protocol selection
Custom Base URL and exact-origin permission
API Key scope and capability fingerprint
Connection tests, errors, disclosure and Options UX

constraints: P1, P3 and P4 bundles must be complete.
Ordinary users see AI service, model, API Key and Test connection only.
Protocol and Base URL appear only under Custom advanced settings.
Custom dispatches to Chat or Responses adapters.
A provider/origin change invalidates saved-key eligibility; a same-origin protocol change may retain the key but clears capability readiness.
Custom permission is requested for the exact canonical origin from an explicit user gesture.
API keys and secrets are excluded from logs, errors, chat and exports.
Arbitrary additional headers are out of v1.

requirements.text: Separate user-facing service identity from adapter protocol and dispatch through one registry.
Add native OpenAI, OpenRouter and Anthropic profiles with safe defaults and connection probes.
Allow Custom advanced settings to select Chat Completions or Responses and configure Base URL.
Preserve exact-origin permissions, credential scope, disclosure and capability invalidation rules.
Expose clear loading, success and bounded error states without protocol jargon in the default UI.

acceptance_criteria.text: Each service/profile resolves deterministically to one verified adapter, endpoint, headers and identity version; Custom never creates a fourth adapter.
acceptance_criteria.proof: Registry and dispatch matrix tests pass.

acceptance_criteria.text: OpenAI, OpenRouter and Anthropic connection tests validate text plus a named tool round-trip with protocol-specific errors and narrow host access.
acceptance_criteria.proof: Controlled connection-test fixtures and manifest checks pass.

acceptance_criteria.text: Custom users can select Chat or Responses and a valid Base URL; the chosen existing adapter receives the canonical endpoint.
acceptance_criteria.proof: Options, normalization and endpoint tests pass for both protocols.

acceptance_criteria.text: Keys never cross provider/origin, protocol changes clear stale capability readiness, exact Custom origin permission is required, and disclosure follows service/origin changes.
acceptance_criteria.proof: Credential, capability, disclosure and permission regression tests pass.

acceptance_criteria.text: Default Options shows only service, model, API Key and Test connection; advanced protocol terms are confined to Custom and all errors remain bounded and secret-free.
acceptance_criteria.proof: English/Chinese Options interaction and redaction tests pass.

design.summary: Represent service identity and protocol separately. Native services select a fixed adapter profile; Custom explicitly selects one existing OpenAI protocol adapter.
boundaries: Auth store owns credential scope and capability readiness.
Provider gate owns disclosure, permission and connection probes.
Options owns user configuration and errors.
contracts: OpenAI defaults to Responses after P3 verification.
compatibility: Normalize missing Custom protocol to Chat for current unreleased data.
Revise the unreleased config shape in place rather than add a speculative migration.
Keep current provider/origin credential scope semantics.
Keep Auto Tags independent of provider configuration.
rollout: Register native profiles and connection probes.
Update permissions, disclosure, copy and release tests.
rollback: Unknown profiles normalize to non-ready and require a new connection test.
Individual native profiles can be removed without changing adapters.
observability: Record service, protocol, model, connection phase, latency and bounded error category.
Never record keys, headers, request bodies or response text.

principles: Keep protocols out of the default user path.
Reuse adapters rather than multiply provider implementations.
Treat permissions and credentials as application-owned security boundaries.
drivers: Custom must support both requested OpenAI protocol families.
Connection tests and capability proofs are protocol-specific.
Chrome host permissions and keys must remain origin-bound.

options.summary: Treat Custom as a fourth adapter.
costs: Duplicates Chat/Responses parsing and drifts from protocol fixes.
options.invalidation_reason: It creates duplicated protocol implementations and inconsistent safety behavior.

options.summary: Model Custom as configuration selecting Chat or Responses.
benefits: One implementation per protocol and consistent tests.
costs: Registry and capability identity must include protocol.

consequences: Custom is not counted among the three adapters.
Protocol is persisted only where selection is user-configurable.
A protocol change requires capability revalidation.

steps.text: Add service/protocol types, endpoint profiles, normalization and registry dispatch.
Register native OpenAI, OpenRouter and Anthropic profiles, headers, permissions and connection probes.
Add Custom Chat/Responses advanced settings and canonical endpoint handling.
Lock credential, capability, disclosure, permission, error, i18n and DESIGN.md contracts.

verification.procedure: Run service/protocol normalization, endpoint, identity and adapter dispatch matrix tests.
Run controlled named-tool connection tests for native OpenAI, OpenRouter and Anthropic profiles and inspect manifest host patterns.
Run Custom Chat/Responses Options, endpoint, permission and connection tests.
Run credential scope, capability fingerprint, disclosure invalidation, exact-origin permission and secret-redaction regressions.
Run Options English/Chinese tests, pnpm typecheck, pnpm test:logic and agent release gates.

risks.risk: A key is reused for a different service or origin.
risks.trigger: Registry changes weaken credential eligibility checks.
risks.mitigation: Keep provider+origin scope and test every switch path.

risks.risk: A protocol change reuses stale capability proof.
risks.trigger: Protocol/path/profile is absent from the fingerprint.
risks.mitigation: Include protocol identity and clear readiness on change.

risks.risk: Custom permissions become broader than the configured service.
risks.trigger: Runtime relies on optional all-host declaration without exact-origin checks.
risks.mitigation: Request and revalidate the canonical origin immediately before fetch.

risks.trigger: v1 accepts free-form header names and values.
risks.mitigation: Keep arbitrary headers out of v1 and use protocol-owned headers plus API Key only.

risks.risk: Dirty shared files cause lost changes during integration.
risks.trigger: P1 or P5 edits provider/config files concurrently in the same worktree.
risks.mitigation: Preserve the current baseline and sequence shared-file changes or integrate isolated worktrees deliberately.
